paragraphs: i/y— JJ earing of the arrival of the Bharata with the army Gargya and Yudhajit, the king of Kekayas, w'ere greatly delighted. And with a huge army they speedily went out for conquering the Gandharbas. Thereupon the highly pow'erful and light-armed Bharata and Yudhajit, with the soldiers and followers, arrived at the city of Gandharbas. Having heard of the coming of Bharata the highly powerful Gandharbas gathered round and sent up leonine roars. Thereupon began the battle capable of making down erect and continued for a week. On neither side there was victory RAMA YANA. or defeat. On all sides there flowed streams of bloocf and there were afloat human bodies. Daggers, Saktis ancf bows were like the banks of the river.

Thereupon enraged Bharata, Rama’s younger brother, discharged a dreadful arrow named Sangharata resembling the fire of dissolution against Gandharbas. Having bound them all with the noose of death and sundered theni with Sangharata, Bharata despatched all the Gan-dharbas to the abode of death. Even the celestials could not recolTect if such a dreadful encounter had happerjed before. In a moment the huge Gandharba host was slain. After the destruction of the Gandharbas, Kaikey^s son Bharata set up two excellent and prosperous cities in the province of Gandharba. And he placed Taksha in Takshasila and Pushkala in Pushkalabati. Both the cities were filled with profuse riches and jewels and- covered with various gardens. As for many ornaments both of them as if vied with one another.

By just purchases and sales,, and by the conduct of the people the cities grew highly charming. Both of them w'ere filled with gardens and conveyances. Rows of shops were well arranged by the streets in both the cities. Both of them were adorned with many excellent fancy articles, picturesque houses, charming palaces and many beautiful and high Tala,. Tamala, Tilaka and Vakula trees. Having reared up those two cities within five years, Rama’s younger brother, the mighty armed Bharata, son of Kaikeyi, returned to Ajodhya. And like unto Vasava saluting Brahma he adored the hierfisouled Raghava the very personation of virtue and communicated unto him duly the destruction of the Gandharbas and the establishment of the two cities. And hearing the words of Bharata, RSma attained to an excess of delight. UTTA RA KAN DA M.

verses.sa:
श्रुत्वा सेनापतिं प्राप्तं भरतं केकयाधिपः ।
युधाजिद्गार्ग्यसहितं परां प्रीतिमुपागमत् ॥

स निर्ययौ जनौघेन महता केकयाधिपः ।
त्वरमाणो ऽभिचक्राम गन्धर्वान्कामरूपिणः ॥

भरतश्च युधाजिच्च समेतौ लघुविक्रमैः ।
गन्धर्वनगरं प्राप्तौ सबलौ सपदानुगौ ॥

श्रुत्वा तु भरतं प्राप्तं गन्धर्वास्ते समागताः ।
योद्धुकामा महावीर्या व्यनदन् वै समन्ततः ॥

ततः समभवद्युद्धं तुमुलं रोमहर्षणम् ।
सप्तरात्रं महाभीमं न चान्यतरयोर्जयः ॥

खड्गशक्तिधनुर्ग्राहा नद्यः शोणितसंस्रवाः ।
नृकलेवरवाहिन्यः प्रवृत्ताः सर्वतोदिशम् ॥

ततो रामानुजः क्रुद्धः कालस्यास्त्रं सुदारुणम् ।
संवर्तं नाम भरतो गन्धर्वेष्वभ्यचोदयत् ॥

ते बद्धाः कालपाशेन संवर्तेन विदारिताः ।
क्षणेनाभिहतास्तेन तिस्रः कोट्यो महात्मनाम् ॥

तं घातं घोरसङ्काशं न स्मरन्ति दिवौकसः ।
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण तादृशानां महात्मनाम् ॥

हतेषु तेषु सर्वेषु भरतः केकयीसुतः ।
निवेशयामास तदा समृद्धे द्वे पुरोत्तमे ॥

तक्षं तक्षशिलायां तु पुष्कलं पुष्कलावते ।
गन्धर्वदेशे रुचिरे गान्धारविषये च सः ॥

उभे पुरवरे रम्ये विस्तरैरुपशोभिते ।
गृहमुख्यैः सुरुचिरैर्विमानसमवर्णिभिः ॥

सो ऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं साक्षाद्धर्ममिवापरम् ।
राघवं भरतः श्रीमान्ब्रह्माणमिव वासवः ॥

शशंस च यथावृत्तं गन्धर्ववधमुत्तमम् ।
निवेशनं च देशस्य श्रुत्वा प्रीतो ऽस्य राघवः ॥
